beats.text: Same robot, same two kilogram block, same push. Only the surface changes.
Left: a rough, rubbery mat. Right: a smooth one, like ice.
Watch the force graph. Rough: about fourteen newtons, and bumpy.
Smooth: under one newton, and flat.
Sliding friction is roughly mu times the normal force. Same block, so the effort scales with mu: about twenty times more on the rough surface.
The bumps come from stick slip: the surfaces grip, let go, and grip again.
For a robot, that means more motor effort, more vibration, and harder force control.
